written.myAnswer: Lower molecular mass covalent compounds have weak intermolecular attractions, so little energy is needed to separate their molecules. They are therefore often gases or low-boiling liquids.
Many covalent compounds are non-polar, whereas water is polar, so they generally do not dissolve in water and are often more soluble in non-polar solvents.

Iodine molecules are larger than Cl₂ molecules, so the intermolecular attractions between iodine molecules are stronger. More energy is needed to separate them, making iodine a solid while chlorine is a gas under ordinary conditions.

Ionic compounds consist of oppositely charged ions in a crystal lattice; covalent compounds mostly consist of discrete neutral molecules. Ionic compounds generally have high melting and boiling points, are often soluble in water, and conduct electricity when molten or dissolved because their ions can move. Molecular covalent compounds generally have lower melting and boiling points, are often insoluble in water but soluble in non-polar solvents, and usually do not conduct electricity.
